As shown in the figure, an electric lamp weighing $10\mathrm{N}$ is suspended by light ropes $A O$ and $B O$ in a stationary state. The angle $\alpha$ between rope $A O$ and the vertical direction is always $30^{\circ}$, while the angle $\beta$ between rope $B O$ and the vertical direction can vary.

1. When the angle $\beta$ between the rope $BO$ and the vertical direction is $30^{\circ}$, what is the magnitude of the tension force $F_{1}$ in the rope $BO$?
2. Keep the lamp stationary, and slowly adjust the direction of rope $BO$ until the tension is minimized. At this point, what is the angle $\beta$ between rope $BO$ and the vertical direction? What is the magnitude of the minimum tension $F_{2}$?

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an electric lamp weighing $10\mathrm{N}$ is suspended by light ropes $AO$ and $BO$ in a stationary state. The angle $\alpha$ between rope $AO$ and the vertical direction is always $30^{\circ}$, while the angle $\beta$ between rope $BO$ and the vertical direction can vary. 1. When the angle $\beta$ between rope $BO$ and the vertical direction is $30^{\circ}$, what is the magnitude of the tension force $F_1$ in rope $BO$? 2. Keep the lamp stationary, and slowly adjust the direction of rope $BO$ until the tension is minimized. At this point, what is the angle $\beta$ between rope $BO$ and the vertical direction? What is the magnitude of the minimum tension $F_2$?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, two light ropes AO and BO intersect at point O and suspend an electric lamp, and the electric lamp is directly below point O. At point O there is a vertical dashed line as the vertical reference direction; the angle between the left rope AO and the vertical direction is labeled α, and the angle between the right rope BO and the vertical direction is labeled β. The problem gives that the weight of the electric lamp W = 10 N, and α = 30°, while β is variable.

Reasoning: Let the tension in AO be T_A, and the tension in BO be T_B. Point O is at rest, and the forces are balanced in the horizontal and vertical directions:
T_A sin α = T_B sin β,
T_A cos α + T_B cos β = 10.

1. When β = 30°, and α = 30°, from horizontal equilibrium we know T_A = T_B. In the vertical direction: 2T_B cos30° = 10, so T_B = 10/(2 × √3/2) = 10/√3 = 10√3/3 N. Therefore F_1 = 10√3/3 N.

2. When β is variable, from horizontal equilibrium we get T_A = T_B sinβ / sin30° = 2T_B sinβ. Substituting into vertical equilibrium: 2T_B sinβ cos30° + T_B cosβ = 10, that is, T_B(√3 sinβ + cosβ) = 10. Because √3 sinβ + cosβ = 2sin(β + 30°), T_B = 10/[2sin(β + 30°)] = 5/sin(β + 30°). To make T_B minimum, sin(β + 30°) needs to be maximum, and the maximum value is 1, so β + 30° = 90°, β = 60°. At this time the minimum tension F_2 = 5 N.
